text.p: Pen pictures of players expected to comprise the Liverpool squad for Saturday's English premier league match against Manchester United:
David James. Goalkeeper. Age 26. Has moved into contention for an England place behind David Seaman and Ian Walker and improving all the time, with his well-documented mistakes becoming rarer.

Mark Wright. Defender. Age 33. Injury cost him a place in Euro 96 but the England defender has recovered and, after losing his place two seasons ago, is now an integral part of coach Roy Evans's defensive system.
Neil Ruddock. Defender. Age 28. Will recieve a torrid reception from United fans if he plays after being involved in the incident in which Andy Cole's legs were broken in a reserve match last week.

Stig Inge Bjornebye. Defender. Age 26. One injury after another restricted him to just 53 league appearances in almost four years at Liverpool. Now fit, he is justifying the club's faith in him with some excellent early-season performances.
John Scales. Defender. Age 29. Currently in the squad but out of the side. Urbane and articulate off the pitch, intelligence and speed are his main assets on it.
Phil Babb. Defender. Age 25. Now in his third season at Anfield and recently scored his first goal for Liverpool against his former club Coventry.

Jason McAteer. Midfield. Age 24. Childhood dream came true when he completed his 4.5million ($7.0 million) switch from Bolton a year ago. Now established in right-sided role and an extra attacking weapon. But defensively is suspect and will find Giggs a real problem.
Michael Thomas. Midfield. Age 28. There have been rumours of a transfer for months -- but he's still in there battling away in the Liverpool midfield.

Jamie Redknapp. Midfield. Age 22. Lost five months of last season then the opening weeks of the current season with various injuries. Not yet fully fit, but back in contention in the squad. Son of West Ham manager Harry Redknapp.

John Barnes. Midfield. Age 32. The former wing sensation who will 33 next month has evolved into a more cerebral midfield passer, leaving others to do the running. Retains the ability to alter the tempo of a game and a key player in Liverpool's good start to the season.
Steve McManaman. Winger. Age 24. One of the successes of Euro 96. Runs freely, passes well, scores, and is the cornerstone of most of Liverpool's attacks.

Robbie Fowler. Striker. Age 21. Scored both goals for Liverpool at Old Trafford last season and one against United at Liverpool. Has the true striker's ability to score despite a poor performance but been relatively quiet so far this season.

Stan Collymore. Striker. Age 25. Big Stan has never seemed truly happy at Anfield, looking weighed down by his 8.5 million pounds fee at the start of last season and now left out to make way for new Czech signing Patrik Berger this season.

Patrik Berger, Striker. Age 22. The Czech has made a great impact at Anfield since moving from Borussia Dortmund, with five goals in his opening three matches for Liverpool, including two superb solo efforts against Chelsea. Should relish the occasion.

REFEREE: David Elleray. A 42-year-old school teacher, he has been rated the best referee in the premier league despite having dismissed four players and booked 15 so far this season. He booked 10 players in the Euro 96 first round match between Germany and the Czech Republic.
